headword: {草食動物|そうしょくどうぶつ}

definitions.explanation: An animal that feeds primarily on plants. Also used figuratively (especially 草食系) to describe a passive, unassertive person, particularly in the context of romantic relationships.

examples.japanese: ⟦{牛|うし}→牛：01857_ushi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草食動物|そうしょくどうぶつ}だ。
{草食動物|そうしょくどうぶつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{植物|しょくぶつ}→植物：03248_shokubutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べて→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{生|い}きている→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧。
⟦サバンナ→サバンナ：28719_sabanna⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{草食動物|そうしょくどうぶつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{肉食動物|にくしょくどうぶつ}→肉食動物：18131_nikushokudoubutsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{狙|ねら}われる→狙う：00313_nerau⟧。
examples.english: On the savanna, herbivores are targeted by carnivores.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{草食|そうしょく}→草食：20954_soushoku⟧ (herbivorous, plant-eating) and ⟦{動物|どうぶつ}→動物：01480_doubutsu⟧ (animal). A standard biological term that has also taken on cultural significance in modern Japanese.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The term ⟦{草食系|そうしょくけい}→草食系：27138_soushokukei⟧ (herbivore type) became a widely-used buzzword describing men (and sometimes women) who are passive, gentle, and uninterested in actively pursuing romantic relationships. The contrasting term is ⟦{肉食系|にくしょくけい}→肉食系：24331_nikushokukei⟧ (carnivore type) for aggressive, assertive pursuers.
